reviewContext.issueReference: Work Runtime P1-6c; no GitHub issue supplied
reviewContext.userProblem: SIGINT or external cancellation can commit after ordinary terminal-session persistence but before task reconciliation, leaving a pending request that cannot be acknowledged against the exact cancelled session.
requiredOutcomes: Use a shared SQLite transaction to arbitrate cancellation insertion against canonical terminal persistence, including both snapshot save overloads and every task-backed terminal writer.
Request-first retains a durable decision, interrupts and joins owned work, persists exact cancelled stop proof, acknowledges once, and preserves fencing and replay.
Terminal-first rejects new cancellation without decision, request, application or version mutation; late SIGINT preserves ordinary success or failure and reconciliation.
Prove both orderings for SIGINT and external cancellation with deterministic barriers at production boundaries, plus independent-connection store tests and the real EntryPoint SIGINT regression.

Produce final-source build, focused tests, SwiftLint, manifest, capable-host focused and serial aggregate logs with exact exits and positive counts; obtain independent integrity, adversarial and Astra acceptance before documentation and implementation publication.
nonGoals: P1-6d, P1-7a/b, parent P1 completion, unrelated baseline repairs, new store/schema/scheduler, decision-row mutation, hidden cleanup after success, main merge or release.
constraints: Preserve checkpoint 2e7a264 and all tracked/untracked P1-6c WIP; one serial owner edits coupled Swift paths, with independent read-only reviews.
Use only the immutable user-scope codex-design-and-implement-review-loop; no reset, force push, broad staging, concurrent Git writes or scratch outside repository tmp/.
Prior focused 99/99 and aggregate 2049/19 logs are historical after Swift changes; sandbox listener denials are environmental failures, and broad aggregate stays FAILED until it passes.
Protect Monja and other worktrees; keep 19 non-slice aggregate failures with explicit owners.
designDecisionsAndRationale: The shared runtime SQLite commit is the linearization point because attempt reconciliation and process-local observation can lag canonical session persistence.
Cancellation insertion reads the exact reserved canonical session inside its write transaction; terminal save checks pending cancellation in its snapshot transaction, so only one ordering commits.
Request-first returns control to owned shutdown for exact stop proof; terminal-first produces an explicit already-terminal outcome without changing the ordinary result.
Accepted decision replay precedes new-request validation; stale live saves cannot replace a terminal winner; task-free workflows retain current behavior.
intentionalTradeoffs: Keep one serial implementation plan for coupled store, runner, CLI and test changes; independent reviewers inspect frozen bytes without overlapping writes.
Historical contradictory records fail closed for diagnosis, without retroactive cleanup.
Listener-dependent focused and aggregate verification requires a capable host; sandbox failures remain recorded as failures.
supportedEdgeCases: SIGINT and external cancel, each request-first and terminal-first; SIGINT between observer join and final signal commit.
Ordinary success and failure, accepted-decision replay, repeated late rejection, both cancellation insertion APIs and independent SQLite connections.
Both canonical snapshot save overloads, delayed live save, selected-host stop proof, failed persistence, lost acknowledgment, prelaunch cancellation, exact identity and fencing.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Unrelated P1 slices, unrelated aggregate failures, historical data repair, new task scheduler or registry repair, Monja and other worktrees.
